The Brief

The Fed Turns Hawkish. Chips Rip to a Record Anyway.

01   This Week

Five Moves Reshaping Institutional Positioning.

Rolling window to 18 June 2026 · sourced from Reuters, CNBC, Bloomberg, WSJ, Parallax

• The Fed Holds, but Warsh Rewrites the Script Toward Hikes

The FOMC kept the target at 3.50–3.75% at Kevin Warsh's first meeting but stripped the easing bias from a dramatically shorter statement. The dot-plot 2026 median rose to 3.8% from 3.4%; nine of eighteen officials now see at least one hike, and futures moved the next-move bet toward an October hike. Stocks fell Wednesday, with the S&P 500 −1.21% to 7,420.

• Chips Close the Week at a SOX Record; Intel Rips on an Apple Deal

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ran more than 6% to a record into Thursday and the Nasdaq rallied roughly 2% on the 17th as chips powered a comeback from the Fed selloff. Intel jumped about 9% after President Trump said Apple agreed to design and build chips with Intel in the US. Parallax: US Semiconductor Equipment and Design +5.6% on the 18th, the top daily basket.

• The 2-Year Yield Spikes the Most Since 2008 on a Fed Meeting Day

The 2-year Treasury yield jumped more than 16bp Wednesday, its biggest Fed-day move since March 2008, as Warsh delivered a strict, orthodox message on inflation and traders repriced the path higher; it held near 4.18% Thursday while the 10-year hovered roughly 4.45%. Goldman expects continued front-end volatility.

• Gold Holds Near Recent Highs as Miners Trade Like Meme Stocks

Spot gold rose 3.2% Monday to roughly $4,375, its highest since 9 June, though still about 20% below January's record above $5,589. Bullion and miners surged to records then whipsawed; Barclays called the recent sell-off a reset and stayed constructive. Parallax: Australia Junior Gold Miners +10.7% WTD, among the week's top baskets, though the miner leg faded late.

• Oil Slides Toward $79 as the Strait of Hormuz Reopens

August Brent fell to roughly $79.49 as an interim US–Iran deal reopened the Strait of Hormuz, with tankers carrying more than 12 million barrels crossing and focus shifting to the demand outlook; OPEC+ added 188,000 bpd for June. Parallax: US Oilfield Services and Drilling −8.3% WTD, the weakest US basket.

04   Your Factor Exposure

Based on Live Parallax Telemetry Across 62K Securities.

The Hawkish Turn Is the Real Regime Change

Data: The dot-plot median jumped to 3.8% and the 2-year spiked 16bp Wednesday, its biggest Fed-day move since 2008, yet the rotation book returned +1.79% over 15 to 18 Jun vs ACWI −0.19%.

Implication: The risk is concentrated in a leadership that thinned to 10 of 39 markets green; run a factor-drift check against a higher-for-longer path.

Semis Did the Heavy Lifting, but Narrowly

Data: The SOX hit a record and US Semiconductor Equipment was the top daily basket (+5.6%), while South Korea's Cyclical Value Rotation fell −5.9% WTD on a +77% YTD base.

Implication: That is money hiding in AI-adjacent momentum, not broad risk appetite; single-leadership exposure is path-dependent here.

Energy and Rate-Sensitive Property Funded the Move

Data: US Oilfield Services −8.3% WTD was the weakest US basket as Brent slid toward $79, and Hong Kong property developers fell −7.3% WTD as the front end repriced.

Implication: A book leaning on duration for ballast is fighting the new dot plot; check both the energy and rate-sensitivity exposures.
